newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kansai Electric to build 1.2 trln yen power plant.
newsitem.headline: Kansai Electric to build 1.2 trln yen power plant.

text.p: Kansai Electric Power Co said on Wednesday it would start a 1.2 trillion yen project to build a 4.4 million kilowatt (kw) thermal power station in western Japan's Wakayama Prefecture.

The firm aims to put the first generator at the plant on line by November 2006 and all four generators, each with a capacity of 1.1 million kw, would be up and running by 2015, a company spokesman said.
The generators will run mainly on orimulsion, a tar-like fuel made up of water and bitumen.
The firm will build the plant adjacent to its existing 1.8 million kw fuel oil-fired power plant on the coast at Gobo, in Wakayama prefecture in central Japan, the spokesman said.
Kansai Electric hopes to receive government approval for the plant by next March, he said.

The company also plans to build a 3.7 million kw thermal power plant, which will run on liquefied natural gas, in Wakayama city. The first generator at this plant is expected to be in operation by 2004, he said.
